rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far argues that the emigrants are free and have shed no blood unjustly; he also denies unlawful taking of property, while Quraysh seek their return only because they changed religions.
rows.anchor: فقال جعفر سلهما هل أرقنا دما بغير حق فيقتص منا؟ فقال عمرو لا ولا قطرة

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far contrasts their former worship of stones and disbelief with Islam, brought by God's Messenger in a scripture that agrees with Jesus' Gospel.
rows.anchor: فقال جعفر أما الدين الذي كنا عليه فهو دين الشيطان كنا نكفر بالله ونعبد الحجارة

rows.speaker: النجاشي
rows.claim: Najashi asks the priests whether a messenger would come between Jesus and the Hour; they affirm the promise, and he says belief in that messenger entails belief in him.
rows.anchor: قال النجاشي أنشدكم بالله الذي أنزل الإنجيل على عيسى هل تجدون بين عيسى وبين يوم القيامة نبيا مرسلا؟

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far describes the Qur'an, moral conduct, good neighborliness, kinship, care for orphans, and worship of God alone; the recitation moves Najashi and his priests to tears.
rows.anchor: فقال النجاشي لجعفر ما ذا يقول لكم هذا الرجل؟ وما يأمركم به؟ وما ينهاكم عنه؟ فقال يقرأ علينا كتاب الله

rows.speaker: النجاشي
rows.claim: After hearing Mary's and Jesus' story, Najashi says Christ taught no more than Ja'far's account and gives the Muslims safe asylum.
rows.anchor: فلما أتى على ذكر مريم وعيسى رفع النجاشي من سواكه قدر ما يقذي العين وقال والله ما زاد المسيح على ما تقولون هذا

rows.speaker: النجاشي
rows.claim: Najashi identifies Ja'far's party and Muhammad as Abraham's party, then returns Quraysh's gifts as a bribe, saying God made him king without taking a bribe.
rows.anchor: فلا دهورة اليوم على حزب إبراهيم فقال عمرو يا نجاشي ومن حزب إبراهيم؟ قال هؤلاء الرهط

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far's account says God revealed the verse about the people nearest Abraham in connection with their dispute over Abraham.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر فانصرفنا فكنا في خير جوار وأنزل الله عز وجل في ذلك على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في خصومتهم في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the long Najashi account is transmitted through other routes, including the Ahl al-Bayt, and is valuable for the early emigrants' trials, but is not an occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: وليست من سبب النزول في شيء

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ali explains that Abraham was neither a Jew praying westward nor a Christian praying eastward, but a hanif Muslim following Muhammad's religion.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين لا يهوديا يصلي إلى المغرب ولا نصرانيا يصلي إلى المشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i takes the report's reference to Muhammad's religion as facing the Kaaba after the qibla changed in Medina; Jews and Christians turned away from that central direction.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتبر في الرواية استقبال الكعبة وقد حولت القبلة إليها في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the description of the qibla as a middle direction is a subtle interpretive allusion, not more than that.
rows.anchor: فإنما هي عناية لطيفة لا تزيد على ذلك

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq glosses hanif as wholly sincere, with no element of idol worship.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام خالصا مخلصا ليس فيه شيء عن عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ali says those nearest the prophets are the people who most act upon their teaching; Muhammad's ally obeys God despite distant kinship, while his enemy disobeys despite close kinship.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن أولى الناس بالأنبياء أعملهم بما جاؤوا به

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies those nearest Abraham as the Imams and their followers.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام هم الأئمة ومن اتبعهم

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: In reports through Ibn Udhaynah, al-Sadiq tells him three times that he and his addressees are from the family of Muhammad, of their own selves.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن أذينة عنه عليه السلام قال أنتم والله من آل محمد فقلت من أنفسهم جعلت فداك؟

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says Jews were pleased when Muhammad first prayed toward Jerusalem, then opposed the change to the Kaaba at the noon prayer and urged morning belief followed by evening disbelief to mislead Muslims.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لما قدم المدينة وهو يصلي نحو بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i reads wajh al-nahar in the report as modifying what was revealed, rather than the command to believe, and notes that he discussed this earlier.
rows.anchor: والرواية كما ترى تجعل قوله وجه النهار ظرفا لقوله أنزل دون قوله آمنوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews told Muslims to profess belief in Muhammad in the morning and return to their own prayer at day's end, hoping Muslims would regard Jews as more learned and abandon their faith; al-Suddi and Mujahid also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { وقالت طائفة } قال إن طائفة من اليهود قالت إذا لقيتم أصحاب محمد أول النهار فآمنوا

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says the warning about trading God's covenant and oaths for a small price was revealed concerning the covenant; khalaq means one's share, and without an afterlife share one cannot enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام قال أنزل في العهد { إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا

rows.speaker: والد عدي بن عدي
rows.claim: Adi ibn Adi's father recounts that a man disputing land before the Prophet returned it after being warned of the punishment for claiming it by a false oath.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن عدي عن أبيه قال اختصم امرؤ القيس ورجل من حضرموت إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the land-dispute report does not establish that the verse was revealed for that case; Sunni reports conflict over the parties and circumstances.
rows.anchor: والرواية كما ترى لا تدل على نزول الآية في مورد القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports variously place the dispute between al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and a Jewish man, or describe a disbelieving seller falsely swearing about a market item's price to deceive a Muslim.
rows.anchor: وفي بعضها أنه كان بين الأشعث بن القيس وبين رجل من اليهود في أرض له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the verse's role as an explanation of the preceding verse, he prefers reading the reports, where possible, as examples to which the warning applies rather than as revelation occasions.
rows.anchor: فالوجه حمل الروايات إن أمكن على بيان انطباق الآية على مورد القصة دون النزول بالمعنى المعهود منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses form a second argument defending Jesus from Christian claims: he is neither God nor someone who claimed divinity, since he is a created human, born and raised by his mother, though fatherless like Adam.
rows.anchor: بيان وقوع الآيات عقيب الآيات المرتبطة بأمر عيسى عليه السلام يفيد أنها بمنزلة الفصل الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human given scripture, judgment, and prophethood remains a servant; such a prophet cannot claim worship or give another creature a right to worship that belongs to God, nor deny a prophet's God-given right.
rows.anchor: والنبي الذي هذا شأنه لا يعدو طور العبودية ولا يتعرى عن زي الرقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar is synonymous with insan and can denote either one human being or a group.
rows.anchor: البشر مرادف للإنسان، ويطلق على الواحد والكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ma kāna li-bashar denotes ownership or entitlement: the human has no right to do this, as in the cited Qur'anic formulations.
rows.anchor: اللام للملك أي لا يملك ذلك أي ليس له بحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God granting scripture, judgment, and prophethood is the subject of kāna and prepares for the following clause; its inclusion signals that divine grant itself is central.
rows.anchor: اسم كان إلا أنه توطئة لما يتبعه من قوله { ثم يقول للناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' denial that he could say what he had no right to say illustrates that God's prophetic gifts and education prevent their recipient from claiming worship.
rows.anchor: قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying only that a human may not claim worship would mean a legal prohibition despite possible sin; the wording that God grants him scripture and prophethood makes the claim impossible under divine guidance.
rows.anchor: فإن العبارة الثانية تفيد معنى أصل التشريع كما تقدم بخلاف قوله { أن يؤتيه الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's nurturing purpose does not fail; those granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood are not abandoned even if others disbelieve, as another verse states.
rows.anchor: فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means a human cannot receive these divine gifts and then call people to worship himself instead of God.
rows.anchor: فمحصل المعنى أنه لا يسع لبشر أن يجمع بين هذه النعم الإلهية وبين دعوة الناس إلى عبادة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context resembles the statement that Christ and the angels are too exalted to disdain God's worship, since such arrogance merits punishment and God would not punish his honored prophets and angels.
rows.anchor: فإن المستفاد من الآية أن المسيح وكذا الملائكة المقربون أجل شأنا وأرفع قدرا أن يستنكفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although thumma usually marks succession, ideas can be considered together even when their events occur successively, so it does not defeat the combined meaning.
rows.anchor: وكما يصح اعتبار الاجتماع والمعية بين المتحدين زمانا كذلك يصح اعتباره بين المترتبين والمتتاليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibad is a plural of abd like abid; ibad is commonly used for servants ascribed to God, while people are usually said to have abid.
rows.anchor: فالعباد كالعبيد جمع عبد، والفرق بينهما أن العباد يغلب استعماله فيما إذا نسب إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min duni Allah necessarily excludes worship directed to another, since God accepts only worship sincerely devoted to him.
rows.anchor: وتقييد قوله عبادا لي بقوله من دون الله تقييد قهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True worship presupposes assigning the worshiped some independence, even in partnership; because God's lordship is absolute, his worship requires denying all independence to everything else, so worshiping another alongside God is worship apart from him.
rows.anchor: فإن الشريك من حيث إنه شريك مساهم ذو استقلال ما، والله سبحانه له الربوبية المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Study is more specific than teaching and usually means learning from a book by reading.
rows.anchor: والدراسة أخص من التعليم فإنه يستعمل غالبا فيما يتعلم عن الكتاب بقراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i cites Qur'anic descriptions of people studying a scripture and of earlier communities studying books given to them.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى { ودرسوا ما فيه }

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says study is more specific than teaching and usually means learning from a book by reading; dars involves taking up a trace through sustained reading and memorization.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب درس الدار بقي أثرها، وبقاء الأثر يقتضي انمحائه في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation calls people to believe certainly in the divine teachings they study, embody their virtues, and practice the good works they teach, thereby becoming God-oriented scholars.
rows.anchor: ومحصل الكلام أن البشر الذي هذا شأنه إنما يدعوكم إلى التلبس بالإيمان واليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense wording hints at an indirect address to Christians: Israel possessed and studied scripture amid alteration, and Jesus came to clarify disputes, ease some prohibitions, and restore their proper teaching and study.
rows.anchor: حيث اشتمل على الماضي الدال على التحقق لا يخلو عن دلالة ما على أن الكلام في الآية مسوق للتعريض بالنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can also apply to Muhammad because his mission addressed scriptural People of the Book, but Jesus fits it first because his mission was specifically to Israel; it does not fit Noah, Abraham, or Moses.
rows.anchor: لكن عيسى عليه السلام أسبق انطباقا عليه، وكانت رسالته خاصة ببني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the well-known reading with ya'murakum in the accusative, the clause about not commanding angels and prophets as lords is coordinated with the preceding verb yaqulu.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله يقول، على القراءة المشهورة التي هي نصب يأمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse counters groups attributing worship of angels to religion, including Sabeans and pagan Arabs who called angels God's daughters while claiming Abraham's faith; it also rejects the Jewish claim that Ezra is God's son, which Moses did not authorize and the Torah does not teach.
rows.anchor: وكعرب الجاهلية حيث كانوا يقولون إن الملائكة بنات الله، وهم يدعون أنهم على دين إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause alludes to Christians' worship of Jesus and their explicit claim that he called them to his divinity; other claims about angels and prophets imply divinity, so the verse says lords rather than gods.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك نسبة منهم إليه أنه قال كونوا عبادا لي بخلاف اتخاذ الملائكة والنبيين أربابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause says people because its verb implies face-to-face speech and its original audience was absent; the second addresses you because commands can reach descendants through their shared community, unlike spoken words.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن الحاضرون في زمن نزول الآية حاضرين إذ ذاك لا جرم قيل ثم يقول للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address covers scriptural claimants to prophethood and Arabs claiming Abrahamic ancestry; hypothetically, accepting this divinely gifted human would make them Muslims, so he could not then command disbelief.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الخطاب أنه متعلق بجميع المنتحلين بالنبوة من أهل الكتاب أو المدعين للانتساب إلى الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here Islam means the monotheistic religion shared by all prophets, as the surrounding verses say, rather than a later narrower usage.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن المراد بالإسلام هو دين التوحيد الذي هو دين الله عند جميع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the verses with Muhammad, citing a report that Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi and a Christian from Najran asked whether he wanted them to worship him; they read the closing phrase as Islam brought by Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض المفسرين أن المراد بقوله تعالى { ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله } إلى آخر الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects this as conflating Qur'anic Islam, the monotheism of all prophets, with the later technical usage among Muslims after revelation.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه خلط بين الإسلام في عرف القرآن وهو دين التوحيد الذي بعث به جميع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's mother vowed her unborn child for service in the sanctuary, expected a boy, grieved at giving birth to a girl, and named her Mary, meaning the female servant; after Imran's death, the priests disputed her care and lots assigned her to Zechariah.
rows.anchor: كانت أم المسيح مريم بنت عمران حملت بها أمها فنذرت أن تجعل ما في بطنها إذا وضعته محررا يخدم المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah kept Mary in a screened sanctuary where she worshiped; she was provided for miraculously and described as righteous, protected, purified, chosen, addressed by angels, and among the obedient.
rows.anchor: فكانت تعبد الله سبحانه فيها، لا يدخل عليها إلا زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Spirit to Mary in human form and announced a son without a father, his future miracles and mission, his support by the Holy Spirit, and his teaching of scripture, wisdom, Torah, and Gospel; she then conceived.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الله تعالى أرسل إليها الروح وهي محتجبة فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' pregnancy, birth, speech, and existence followed ordinary human patterns; his mother's pain and vow of silence are recounted, and her people accuse her before he speaks from the cradle.
rows.anchor: وكان حمله ووضعه وكلامه وسائر شؤون وجوده من سنخ ما عند سائر الأفراد من الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' cradle declaration that he is God's servant, given scripture and prophethood, blessed, prayerful, and dutiful to his mother foreshadows his struggle against injustice and restoration of Moses' law and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكان هذا الكلام منه عليه السلام كبراعة الاستهلال بالنسبة إلى ما سينهض على البغي والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus and Mary grew up and lived as ordinary humans, eating and drinking and experiencing the conditions common to human life.
rows.anchor: ثم نشأ عيسى عليه السلام وشب وكان هو وأمه على العادة الجارية في الحياة البشرية يأكلان ويشربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was sent to Israel with a new law that confirmed Moses while lifting some Torah restrictions, clarified disputes, and announced a later messenger named Ahmad.
rows.anchor: وكان يدعوهم إلى شريعته الجديدة وهو تصديق شريعة موسى عليه السلام إلا أنه نسخ بعض ما حرم في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus performed the announced signs, including creating a bird, healing the blind and leprous, raising the dead, and revealing hidden matters, all by God's permission.
rows.anchor: وأنجز عليه السلام ما ذكره لهم من المعجزات كخلق الطير وإحياء الموتى وإبراء الأكمه والأبرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After losing hope because of Israel's obstinacy, Jesus selected the disciples who believed as helpers for God.
rows.anchor: فانتخب من الشرذمة التي آمنت به الحواريين أنصارا له إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jews sought to kill Jesus, God took and raised him; the Jews were left to suppose that they had killed or crucified him.
rows.anchor: فتوفاه الله ورفعه إليه، وشبه لليهود فمن زاعم أنهم قتلوه
